evals.name: draft-only-by-default
evals.expected_output: Resolves the range from the newest v* tag to HEAD, or says it is using the whole history when there is no version tag. Runs scripts/first-pass.sh, ignores the DROP commits, reads the bodies of the rest, and prints the entry as it would appear in readme.txt with the range and the screen's counts. Writes no file, and offers to write it.

evals.name: write-needs-a-version
evals.expected_output: Does not write, because no version was given for the heading. Says so in one line and prints the draft instead.

evals.name: writes-above-the-previous-heading
evals.expected_output: Inserts a heading of the shape `= Mon D, Version X.Y.Z =` — the release date, a spaced hyphen, the word Version, then the version, with the day unpadded and the month in English — and its bullets, below `== Changelog ==` and above the previous heading. Uses today's date when no --date was passed. Every bullet starts with a hyphen, not an asterisk, and carries exactly one of Added:, Updated: or Fixed:, grouped in that order, and `- Initial release.` under the bare `= 1.0.0 =` is left unlabelled and undated, because 1.0.0 has not been released and has no date to carry. Then checks that the new version is first, that its full heading shape matches exactly once (not merely the version), that the awk check for unlabelled bullets prints nothing, and that git diff --stat names readme.txt alone. Bumps nothing and commits nothing.

evals.name: pro-suffix-from-the-code
evals.expected_output: Decides each ` (Pro)` suffix from BlockRegistry::PRO_BLOCKS and the template catalogue's 'pro' flag, not from the paths the commits touched. A Pro block still earns a bullet because the Free build ships it locked behind a badge. Does not reinstate the path-only test the style file rules out. Keeps the label before the sentence and the (Pro) suffix after its full stop, never using (Pro) in place of a label.

evals.name: drops-what-nobody-notices
evals.expected_output: Drops CI, docs, tests, tooling, generated output, the previous release commit, refactors, and any bug introduced and fixed inside the same range. When that leaves nothing, says 'nothing user-facing to release' with the range it read, and writes no heading.

evals.name: not-a-release
evals.prompt: /yaychangelog 1.1.0 --write and then tag and publish it
evals.expected_output: Writes the entry, then stops: it does not bump the version, build a zip, commit, tag or push. Points at /yayrelease for the release itself.

evals.name: label-from-what-the-owner-sees
evals.expected_output: Picks each label from what the change does to an installation, not from the commit's Conventional Commits type: a feat that alters an existing default is Updated:, and a feature that shipped broken and now works for the first time is Added: rather than Fixed:. Splits a bullet that would need two labels into two. Uses only Added:, Updated: and Fixed: — never New:, Changed:, Improved:, Removed:, Deprecated: or Security: — and writes a removal as Updated:. Writes every bullet with a leading `- `.

evals.name: date-comes-from-the-caller
evals.expected_output: Writes `= Oct 28, 2026 - Version 1.1.0 =` using the date it was given, not today's, because /yayrelease computes the release date once in its preflight so the changelog heading and the tag annotation cannot disagree across midnight. Run without --date it takes today's with LC_ALL=C date +'%b %e, %Y' | tr -s ' ' — LC_ALL=C for the English month, %e rather than the GNU-only %-d, and tr -s to squeeze the padding on days 1 to 9.
